chapter: Lover Man and the postwar years
title: Getting "Lover Man" heard; Ellis Larkins's demo
summary: Publishers resisted; Ellis Larkins made the demo record and a singer submitted it to Decca.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Is that how people... I don't know, it always seems to me...

Oh, we put this boy's name on it, Jimmy Sherman, because he was with the Charioteers, to put it on the Kraft Hall of Fame. Nothing happened. But now at this time, I'm getting stronger. I'm back from Europe. See what I mean? I'm getting stronger, I'm getting around more. So my contacts become more... I go to different singers. Or
they'd come up to you. If someone saw it... Now, the one that made the demonstration record was Ellis Larkins.
Do you mean as a pianist?

Well, I mean, what can I do? I'm in town, out of town, and all... He was the most welcome one, because I mean, his playing is beautiful. And Anne...I forget that girl's name, a White girl -- she was up and coming. I forget her name. She did the lyric, she sang it, and submitted it to the Decca office.
And that's how that came to be. From Lips' theme song to that. You have people with fantasies about the number. "What were you thinking about when you wrote 'Lover Man'?" Oh, I don't know...!
